title: Unified Authorization & Procurement Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide standards for authorization (access & permissions), change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor onboarding, travel policy, and a set of ready-to-use templates. It is intended for all teams that request access, buy services or hardware, change production systems, or manage third-party relationships.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors interacting with company systems or data.
- Covers requester flows, approval matrices, SLOs, minimal evidence requirements, and escalation paths.
- Does not replace security-specific policies (see security-and-compliance space) but operationalizes approval and procurement patterns for day-to-day use.

Principles:
1) Least privilege: grant the minimal access required and review it regularly.
2) Clear ownership: every system, dataset, and purchase must have an identified owner.
3) Evidence-first approvals: approvals require documented justification and, when applicable, a security review.
4) Operational clarity: workflows include SLAs, rollback criteria, and an escalation contact.

1) Access & Permissions
Overview:
- Use the Access Request System (ARS) to request role-based access. Temporary access must include an explicit expiry and owner.
- Service accounts and long-lived keys must be centrally managed and rotated per the Secrets Management Policy.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Requester: provides business justification, approximate duration, and list of resources.
- Resource Owner: reviews and approves with least-privilege adjustments.
- IAM Team: validates cross-account implications and enforces naming/role conventions.

SLOs and SLA:
- Standard access requests: decision within 24 business hours.
- Expedited access (business-critical): decision within 4 hours; approval requires manager + oncall owner sign-off.
- Emergency "break-glass": temporary keys issued by SRE for up to 8 hours; must be recorded in incident log and reviewed within 72 hours.

Access Request Template (example JSON to paste into ARS):
{
  "requester": "alice@redwood.ai",
  "resource": "production-logs-bucket",
  "role_requested": "read-only",
  "business_justification": "Investigating customer production error #12345",
  "duration_hours": "8",
  "owner": "service-platform-team@redwood.ai"
}

Periodic Review:
- Owners must perform access reviews quarterly for high-sensitivity resources and annually for all other resources.
- Audit evidence: review attestation stored in ARS with checkbox and short comment.

2) Change Management
Change Categories:
- Standard change: routine, pre-authorized, low-risk (no downtime).
- Minor change: low risk but non-routine; requires owner approval and CI results.
- Major change: potential user impact or schema/data migration; requires RFC + change window + rollback plan.

Change Approval Steps (numbered):
1) Create RFC in the Change Tracker with summary, owner, impact, and test results.
2) Run preflight CI and performance checks. Attach results.
3) For major changes, schedule a change window and cross-team reviewers.
4) Post-deploy verification checklist and notify stakeholders.
5) Rollback if verification fails within 15 minutes of detection threshold, or follow incident process.

Standard Change Checklist:
- Owner assigned
- Automated tests passed
- Runbook updated
- Stakeholders notified 48 hours prior

SLOs and Windows:
- Routine deploys permitted 24x5; major releases should occur within designated release windows (see eng-platform/release-schedule).

3) Data Management
Data Classification (three tiers):
- Confidential: customer PII, regulated data. Retention: as per contract or regulatory requirement. Encryption: at rest and in transit. Access: owner + security review.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal documents, internal telemetry. Retention: 2 years default.
- Public: marketing assets, public docs.

Retention & Deletion:
- Data retention schedule must be attached to any new dataset creation request.
- Deletion requests go through Data Steward and must be logged.

Minimal Evidence for New Dataset Onboarding:
- Owner, classification level, retention policy, encryption method, access controls, and intended use case.

Data Incident Handling:
- If a data exposure is suspected, notify security@redwood.ai and follow incident-response-security/runbook within 1 hour.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Approval Matrix (high level):
- <= $2,000: direct manager approval.
- $2,001 - $25,000: manager + finance reviewer.
- $25,001 - $250,000: manager + finance + legal (vendor terms).
- > $250,000: executive sponsorship + legal + procurement committee.

Procurement Steps (numbered):
1) Create Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2) Finance validates budget and cost center.
3) Legal reviews terms if > $25k or involves data processing.
4) Procurement issues PO and confirms delivery schedule.

Expense Policy Highlights:
- Corporate card: for travel and low-value purchases; reconcile within 7 days.
- Reimbursements: receipts required for all purchases > $25.
- Per diems: domestic $75/day, international $110/day unless per-country policy applies; exceptions require pre-approval.

Template: Purchase Request (fields)
- requester_email, vendor_name, estimated_cost, budget_code, business_justification, contract_required (yes/no), expected_delivery_date

Emergency Procurement:
- For urgent hardware or vendor work, procurement may issue an emergency PO with provisional approval; post-facto justification required within 5 business days.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding Checklist:
- Contract signed and stored in Contract Repository
- Security questionnaire completed (SSQ) and reviewed by Security team
- Data processing addendum (DPA) if vendor processes customer data
- Assigned vendor owner and escalation contacts

Vendor Risk Scoring (summary):
- Score 0-100 based on: data-sensitivity handling (40%), uptime & SLA (20%), financial stability (15%), compliance certifications (15%), historical incidents (10%).
- Thresholds: 0-39 Low, 40-69 Medium (requires security review), 70-100 High (requires exec sign-off + controls).

Periodic Review:
- Strategic vendors: reviewed semi-annually.
- Low-risk vendors: annually.

Offboarding:
- Remove access, revoke keys, verify data return/destruction, and confirm final invoice. Checklist must be recorded in vendor record.

6) Travel Policy (operational highlights)
Booking & Approvals:
- All travel booked via Company Travel Portal. Manager approval required for any trip.
- International travel requires People Ops notification for visa/support and updated immunization guidance if applicable.

Budgets & Per Diems:
- See Procurement & Expenses section for per diem rates.
- Business-class permitted for flights > 8 hours or with medical/ADA accommodations.

Expense Reconciliation:
- Submit expenses within 14 days of return. Missing receipts require an attestation. Exceptions escalate to manager and finance.

Travel Risk & Duty of Care:
- Managers must provide emergency contact and confirm traveler is registered with People Ops. In case of travel advisories, travel may be restricted.

7) Templates & Forms (available in this page as downloadable attachments)
- Access request JSON template (copy/paste into ARS)
- Purchase Request form (Procurement Portal)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet)
- Change Request (RFC) template
- Post-deploy verification checklist

8) Governance, Metrics & Reporting
Key metrics to report monthly:
- Time to approve access requests (median & 95th percentile)
- Number of emergency break-glass events and their reviews
- Time-to-procure (PO issued from request)
- Vendor risk distribution and overdue reviews

Ownership & Escalation Table (text):
- Access approvals: IAM Team (owner: Marco Silva)
- Procurement requests and POs: Procurement (owner: Alison Reed)
- Vendor security reviews: Security (owner: Dana Kim)
- Travel & per diem exceptions: People Ops (owner: Maya Chen)

9) Change Log & Review Cadence
- This playbook: reviewed annually or after any major regulatory change.
- Ad-hoc updates can be published with owner approval; material changes notify all teams.

Appendix A: Quick-checklists (copyable)
A1. Quick Access Request Checklist:
- Business justification present
- Owner listed
- Duration specified
- Data classification noted (if applicable)

A2. Quick Procurement Checklist:
- Budget confirmed
- Vendor selected and risk score attached
- Contract/legal review scheduled if required

Appendix B: Example Vendor Risk YAML (for reference)
---
vendor: "AcmeCloud"
data_sensitivity: 30  # 0-40 scale
uptime_sla: 99.95
compliance: ["SOC2", "ISO27001"]
financial_score: 12
historical_incidents: 0
final_score: 78
---

Contacts & References:

- Access Request System: /tools/ars
- Contract Repository: /legal/contracts
- Security questionnaires: /security/vendor-ssq

If you have questions or require an exception, contact procurement@redwood.ai or legal@redwood.ai.
